spec_match.rationale: Attribution is context-conditional (installed PWA on macOS), and the probe reads every determining signal from the real APIs: platform, display-mode via reactive matchMedia, Notification support, live permission state via the Permissions API change event, and Badging presence.

interactive.rationale: Two live actions (request permission, fire a real notification) plus two reactive rows that flip without reload when the user installs the app or changes the permission.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index blurb promises live signal reads with reactive updates; delivered.

edge_cases.rationale: Three-way verdict (attributed context / macOS-but-tab / not-macOS) each with accurate consequences; firing without permission reports the real refusal; constructor-throw path handled with the service-worker alternative named.

references.rationale: Feature index cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5863296436666368 plus the Notifications and Badging specs and the enterprise policy.

conformance.rationale: The suite's permission-queryable and display-mode-detectable assertions are this page's rows as self-contained checks — all six pass live on current engines.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 CDP run: platform row read 'Linux → not macOS' with the honest not-macOS verdict; display-mode row 'browser tab'; permission row live 'prompt'; requestPermission resolved 'default' and the fire attempt reported the real refusal. Zero console errors; 0px overflow both classes; screenshots read.

telemetry_health.rationale: notifattr-context-read asserts with the full signal state.

design_system.rationale: Signal table emerald/rose/charcoal states on near-white rows (AA); table scrolls in wrapper; CSS variables only.

accessibility.rationale: Real table with caption and scoped headers; verdict and action output are role=status live regions; native buttons; states carried in text, not colour alone.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Table owns horizontal scroll; 0px page overflow at 360×740 DPR3 and 1280×2000.

openQuestions.title: Capture the attributed-context run on a macOS install
openQuestions.detail: The full verdict path (installed app on macOS with granted permission, notification visibly attributed in Notification Center) needs a real macOS machine; the display-mode row's live flip on install should be captured there too.

guidanceConsulted.query: request permission on user gesture explain before prompt
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Request permissions from explicit user action with context.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Permission request only fires from its labelled button; the page explains what the state gates before asking.

guidanceConsulted.query: live signal table announce state changes
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce reactive state changes as text.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verdict and action outputs are aria-live; signal states are textual.

summary: Verified headlessly (no chrome-devtools-mcp in this cloud session): every signal row read its real value on the Linux sandbox — including the honest not-macOS verdict — and both action paths reported genuine outcomes (permission 'default', fire refused). The macOS-attributed path is the recorded open question.
